## Design

### 2026-10-11 – What worked

**5h**

What worked
The design is settled: ESP32-C3, SSD1351 OLED, battery with a USB-C charger, and a website that sends images and syncs time. The web page was redesigned to look more professional.

What didn't work, or isn't proven

The LED matrix version didn't give you results you liked, so we dropped it.
I haven't tested any code on real hardware. It hasn't been compiled or run, so small fixes may be needed.
The screen-dimming command may not work on some library versions.
It doesn't work on iPhone, because Web Bluetooth needs Chrome on Android or desktop.
The website must be hosted on HTTPS.
The clock resets if the battery dies, so you'd need to sync time again.
Next step: build the prototype and report any errors. today, I have only made the photo and emoji sharing website.

### 2026-10-11 – Today's work on the Lightning Keychain

**2h**

Today's work on the Lightning Keychain

Today I worked on the documentation and hardware design files for the project. I wrote the GitHub README, covering features, the parts list, wiring, setup steps, the Bluetooth protocol, and the roadmap.

When the recruiter asked for PCB files, I checked what the prototype actually has. It uses ready-made modules joined by wires, so no PCB exists yet. I made a wiring diagram image showing every connection between the ESP32-C3, the OLED, the TP4056 charger, the battery, the switch and the button. I also made a KiCad schematic file of the same wiring, which I still need to open in KiCad and check.

I finalised the Arduino firmware so it's ready to upload once the parts arrive, and I looked into how to add photos to the README.

Next steps: upload the files to GitHub, add a photo to the README, test everything when the hardware arrives, and design a real PCB.

I kept it honest: the firmware and website haven't been tested on hardware yet, and the summary says so. If your colleague wants more detail, I can add a short list of the files you made.
